command: import sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'src'); import security_observatory.cli; print('ok')
commands.when_to_run: After Python module edits, before heavier scans or tests.
commands.recovery_hint: If this fails, inspect the import traceback and confirm the command is run from the repo root.
If pytest is missing or the virtualenv is stale, run uv sync --dev from the repo root.

commands.when_to_run: When the Python virtualenv is missing, stale, or lacks test dependencies.
commands.success_signal: uv resolves dependencies and the repo virtualenv can run pytest.
commands.recovery_hint: If uv is unavailable, install or repair uv before running Python tests.

commands.intent: install the Python package in editable mode
commands.when_to_run: Only when the CLI entrypoint or test environment needs local package installation.
commands.success_signal: pip installs security-observatory and exposes the package to the selected Python.
commands.recovery_hint: If pip is missing, use a Python environment with pip or recreate the virtual environment.

commands.when_to_run: Before dashboard UI development when node_modules is absent or stale.
commands.recovery_hint: If npm fails, check Node/npm availability and dashboard-ui/package-lock.json.

commands.when_to_run: After TypeScript or React dashboard edits.
commands.recovery_hint: If dependencies are missing, run dashboard-install first.

commands.when_to_run: After dashboard UI edits that should update bundled static assets.
commands.success_signal: Vite build succeeds and updates built dashboard assets.
commands.recovery_hint: If build fails, run dashboard-lint and inspect dashboard-ui/vite.config.ts and package scripts.

command: import sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'src'); from security_observatory.cli import main; raise SystemExit(main(['doctor']))
commands.when_to_run: When scanner availability or local setup is uncertain.
commands.recovery_hint: This creates the local observatory layout before printing doctor output; if tools are missing, consult docs/setup.md.

commands.intent: run the local quick security scan
commands.when_to_run: Only when the task explicitly requires validating scanner behavior or producing a local security report.
commands.success_signal: Scan completes and writes a normalized report under ~/.security-observatory.
commands.recovery_hint: If security-scan is unavailable, run the Python entrypoint or install the wrapper with the installer after confirming that is appropriate.

commands.when_to_run: Only after desktop launcher, icon, or bundle metadata changes.
commands.recovery_hint: If swiftc is missing, the script may fall back to Chrome launcher; read docs/desktop-launcher.md.

commands.when_to_run: Only after desktop-build when the user wants the installed app refreshed.
commands.recovery_hint: If install target is missing, the script creates ~/Desktop/MyApps or exits for custom targets.

commands.intent: stop warm desktop launcher servers and wrapper windows
commands.when_to_run: After desktop launcher work or before rebuilding/reinstalling if a warm server is running.
commands.success_signal: Prints that servers/windows were stopped, or that nothing was running.
commands.recovery_hint: This intentionally terminates matching local processes; verify the target app before running.

commands.intent: run the read-only MCP adapter for local agents
commands.when_to_run: Only when an MCP client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex) needs read-only access to local scan results. Normally launched by the client per its mcpServers config, not invoked manually.
commands.success_signal: Holds stdio open and responds to JSON-RPC requests; logs go to stderr.
commands.recovery_hint: If startup fails, confirm `uv sync --extra mcp` has been run and the `mcp` Python package is installed. See mcp/README.md.

commands.intent: run the guarded MCP adapter for AI case-resolution write-back
commands.when_to_run: Only when an MCP client needs explicit case-resolution prompt, preview, and apply tools. Prefer the read-only devsec-mcp command unless the user has opted into AI follow-up write-back.
commands.success_signal: Holds stdio open, lists the read-only tools plus case_followup_prompt, preview_case_resolutions, and apply_case_resolutions, and responds to JSON-RPC requests.
commands.recovery_hint: If startup fails, confirm `uv sync --extra mcp` has been run and the `mcp` Python package is installed. Use devsec-mcp for read-only access.
